title: Check: Snapshot Isolation and Lost Updates

questions.prompt: Alice reads account 1 before a $100 transfer and account 2 after it, and sees $900 instead of $1,000. What's that anomaly?
What does snapshot isolation give each transaction?
options: A consistent snapshot of the database as of when it started
A private copy of the disk

questions.prompt: Snapshot isolation is implemented with multi-version concurrency control. What's the acronym? (four letters)
Under MVCC, readers never block writers, and writers never block readers.
Two transactions increment the same counter by reading it, adding 1, and writing it back. One increment disappears. Which fix is simplest?
options: An atomic UPDATE ... SET value = value + 1

questions.prompt: What does SELECT ... FOR UPDATE do?
options: Locks the rows you read until your transaction ends

questions.prompt: UPDATE docs SET content = 'new' WHERE id = 1 AND content = 'old' matches no rows. What does that tell you?
options: Someone else changed it first, so retry

questions.prompt: What does PostgreSQL call its snapshot isolation level? (two words)
